An EF-0 tornado touched down over open country, near Hwy 188 northeast of Taft.

An NWS Storm Survey Crew found evidence of wind damage along Interstate 37 from mile marker 33 to mile marker 27. Several large trees were down along with large metal highway signs. In addition, an 18 wheeler was flipped near Interstate 37 and Highway 188.
Several power poles were blown down along and near Highway 188.

A tracter trailer near Highway 234 and Interstate 37 was blown over. A few power poles were snapped along Highway 234 between Interstate 37 and CR 2015. Several large trees were also downed near CR 2015 and Highway 234.
A local television station video taped a brief tornado on the leading edge of a gust front a few miles northwest of Gregory. The tornado was over open country and no damage was reported.

An 18-wheeler truck on southbound U.S. 77 in Odem was flipped over and blown off road into another 18-wheeler truck on the northbound side. Also, a furniture truck blew off Interstate 37 southwest of Odem.

This tornado formed just south of the intersection of Highway 136 and Highway 188. An RV trailer was blown over and large tree limbs were broken along the path. Three sheds also collapsed. This tornado moved northeast to southwest.
This tornado touched down in an open cotton field in the outer rainbands of Hurricane Dolly. No damage was reported. This tornado moved northeast to southwest.
Straight-line winds blew off a portion of a tin roof to a barn near St. Paul. In addition, severe power poles were blow down.

A large tree was snapped and blown into the side wall of a house.
Several fences and trees were blown down around the Saint Paul area.
Several 12 inch diameter trees were snapped from the wind and one from lightning at Camp Karankawa. Pea-sized hail was also reported.

Two broken power poles on Railroad Street. A stop sign was uprooted along CR 136. Broken power poles were reported at Hwy 181 and CR 3677.
Two power poles were snapped at Bravo Street. A large tree and power pole were snapped at Victoria Street.

A NWS storm survey team concluded winds of up to 75 mph produced damage consistent with straight-line winds in Aransas Pass. A church had a portion of the roof peeled off. A trailer was also flipped over. Numerous large trees were snapped throughout the city.

Ping pong ball sized hail occurred in Aransas Pass. Numerous RVs sustained minor to major damage from the hail located at several RV resorts around Aransas Pass.
Winds blew power pole down on to railroad track near Highway 181 northwest of Taft.
High winds blew a tree onto power lines which started a small fire in Sinton.
A large tree was blown over in Odem with the tree blocking the front door to the house.

Damage to farm equipment sheds and power lines down northeast of Gregory.

NWS storm survey concluded a tornado touched down in an open field south of Highway 35 about 2 miles east of Gregory. The tornado crossed Highway 35 damaging a few power poles. Maximum winds were estimated at 70 mph.

TCOON observation site at Nueces Delta measured a 59 mph wind gust.

Several eyewitnesses observed a tornado near the intersection of State Highway 188 and Farm to Market Road 631. The tornado remained over open field and produced no significant damage or injuries.
Local law enforcement reported a brief touchdown 8 miles north of Taft. No damage was reported.

NWS storm survey revealed a brief EF-0 tornado touched down in the middle of a farm field with no significant damage. The tornado occurred near the intersection of Highway 188 and County Road 29. A photo from storm spotters in the area confirmed the brief tornado.
